messages:
Maya Chen: @here escalated from support - AcmePlatform complaining about sudden p95/p99 latency spikes starting ~03:10 UTC. They see lots of request queuing in our logs and timeouts on user-facing requests. Ticket 98213 linked. Repro steps below.

Maya Chen: Repro steps customer provided:
1) POST /v1/chat with model=redwood-base
2) payload ~600 tokens initial prompt
3) concurrent clients ~25
They say p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.8s, p99 up to 5-8s, started 03:10 UTC and persisted.

Maya Chen: attaching excerpt from their request tracer:
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:21Z] request_id=acme-req-312 status=queued reason=queueing delay_ms=1200 worker=all
[2026-03-15T03:12:22Z] request_id=acme-req-313 status=processing latency_ms=430
[2026-03-15T03:12:27Z] request_id=acme-req-314 status=timeout
```

alerts-bot: :rotating_light: Service: inference-runtime-pool-3 p95 latency > 1.5s (03:11 UTC). Autoscale attempted +1 node but pool at capacity.

Javier Ortiz: @Maya thanks for the heads up — I'm pulling metrics. First thought: admission control hitting concurrency limits or overloaded worker nodes. Can you share the customer's org id + sample request_id? Also any recent rollout to pool-3?

Maya Chen: org=acme, sample request_id=acme-req-312. No recent model rollouts from their account. They are on shared-hosted tier.

Lena Fischer: looking at cluster: pool-3 shows steady CPU/GPU utilization ~92%, memory ~78%. We have many long-running KV cache misses causing larger per-token CPU. There was a config tweak yesterday that reduced max-inflight from 64 -> 48 (PR #4571) to control latency tail on smaller models. That may be too strict under this workload.

Priya Nair: Acme's usage pattern: bursts of small-ish but long-seq chats; they also recently increased concurrency from their side.

Javier Ortiz: ok that aligns. Seems admission control started queuing earlier requests because inflight cap was reached, queue backlog increased -> p95/p99 regression. Quick mitigation options:
- Temporarily increase pool concurrency cap (revert PR) to 64
- Scale up pool-3 by +1 large instance (fast but costs)
- Apply targeted routing: send Acme traffic to another pool with spare capacity
- Enable per-org token-burst throttle to smooth bursts

Lena Fischer: I can roll back the max-inflight change for pool-3 and trigger a +1 node scale. Rolling back config will require a canary deploy to avoid regressions. How urgent?

Maya Chen: Customer impacted (UI errors for some users). They've escalated to their product lead. Need quick mitigation + follow-up.

Javier Ortiz: Action plan now:
1) Lena: can you start a canary rollback of PR #4571 on pool-3 and scale +1 node? (expected 3-7 min)
2) I'll open a temporary route to divert org=acme to pool-4 with spare headroom while we observe
3) Maya/Priya: inform customer of mitigation and ask if they can reduce concurrent clients temporarily
4) Postmortem to determine if config change should be gated by traffic pattern tests

Lena Fischer: starting canary rollback now. Commands:
```
# rollback canary
infra-deploy --pool pool-3 --rollback-pr 4571 --canary 10%
# scale
infra-scale --pool pool-3 --delta +1
```
I'll post logs when canary passes or fails.

Javier Ortiz: I'll create a routing rule to direct org=acme -> pool-4 for the next 30m.

alerts-bot: scale job started for pool-3 job_id=scale-778, canary-deploy job_id=deploy-889

(5m later)

Lena Fischer: canary passed on 10% — rolling to 100% now. New node added, pools show load dropping to 68%.

Lena Fischer: Metrics after changes (03:20 UTC): p95 dropped to ~190ms, p99 ~520ms for acme traffic. Queue length down from 18 -> 2.

Maya Chen: relaying to Acme: temporary mitigation applied (routing + capacity + rollback). They're going to monitor and asked for a follow-up call. :thumbsup:

Priya Nair: we should add a regression test in our admission-control staging harness to simulate many long-seq concurrent chats and run it on config changes. Filing ticket.

Javier Ortiz: Agreed. Follow-ups:
- Postmortem on config change and why rollout targeted pool-3 without traffic-pattern gating (owner: runtime team)
- Add per-org burst smoothing (product + runtime)
- Improve alerts to rate-limit queue growth separately from p95 spikes

Maya Chen: thanks all. Closing this thread for now — will reopen if customer reports new issues. Ticket 98213 updated with mitigation notes and action items.

alerts-bot: Incident resolved? auto-note: p95 back within expected thresholds (03:24 UTC) :white_check_mark:

Lena Fischer: leaving a note: PR #4571 will be reverted in main until we add traffic tests. Will post PR link when ready.

Javier Ortiz: great work — thanks team. :tada:
